text: {"voteValue":"REJECT","rationale":"The architecture is close, but two implementation-critical ambiguities prevent approval. First, stopEpoch is specified as an unsigned 64-bit SQLite value with SQL old+1 arithmetic, yet SQLite INTEGER is signed 64-bit; the schema, encoding, comparison, guarded increment, and actual maximum are therefore not implementable exactly as written. Second, SO_PEERCRED supplies the peer’s effective UID/GID, not a complete supplementary-group authorization set; merely naming privileged Unix groups does not define a mechanically reliable per-RPC membership check for typical human accounts. Specify a signed nonnegative range or fixed-width encoding with exact increment semantics, and define authorization through dedicated effective-GID processes, UID allowlists, or verified /proc peer groups. The zero-effect-consumer and fail-closed persistence boundaries otherwise satisfy the decisive V1C requirements."}
